patterns.description: Bare fossil resource/column names from the Atomic CRM fork (contacts, companies, deals, tags, ...). Lifted verbatim from Story 1.1's AC-14 word-boundary grep.

exemptReasons.location, contacts, responsiveness: public.shadchanim.contacts is a genuine MyShadchan column (a shadchan's own phone/email, jsonb, 01_tables.sql — that file carries the same word and is already in exactFileAllowlist above) — not the fork's retired contacts table. Story 8.2's column-list grant on 06_grants.sql has to spell the column by name; the phrase is specific to that grant's own column list so it cannot mask an unrelated fossil sharing a line with it.

patterns.description: camelCase/PascalCase compounds of the fossil vocabulary a word-boundary grep on the bare word would miss. Lifted verbatim from Story 1.1's AC-14 second grep.

Every spelling of the retired sales/Sale family (renamed to members) — deliberately a bare, case-insensitive substring, not word-bounded: a word-boundary form misses sales_id, salesId, SalesCreate, useGetSalesName, CURRENT_SALE_CACHE_KEY.

exemptReasons.wholesale: English word that merely contains the retired stem; never an identifier.
exemptReasons.supabase/migrations/20260727122733_renam: The rename migration's own immutable filename, quoted verbatim by scripts/check-wave-ownership.test.mjs to prove a migrations glob overlaps a timestamped file; supabase/migrations is deliberately outside scanPaths because applied history cannot be renamed.

patterns.description: The retired children resource in its SQL/route/dataProvider contexts. Deliberately not a bare "children" word — that also matches React's children prop everywhere.

exemptReasons.p_existing_children_note: Story 5.2: create_shidduch()'s parameter for the SUGGESTED PERSON'S own prior children (a shidduch fact), not the retired `children` resource, which is now `singles` (AD-23).
exemptReasons.existing_children_note: Story 5.2: shidduchim column for the suggested person's own prior children — see above.
exemptReasons.no key beyond resource/id/children/class: RecordLink.test.tsx's closed-prop-list test title; `children` here is React's own prop, one of RecordLinkProps' five legitimate keys.
exemptReasons.\"resource\" | \"id\" | \"children\" | \: RecordLink.test.tsx's ExpectedKeys union, which must spell React's `children` prop literally to assert RecordLinkProps has exactly those five keys.
exemptReasons.child_grants: Story 13.1: the real `child_grants` table key, which the FakeRest generator must spell exactly as the database does or the demo provider stops matching the Supabase one. Same status as the already-allowlisted grants.ts/dataProvider.ts; scoped per-file-per-term rather than whole-file so these two generator files stay covered by every other retired-name pattern.
exemptReasons.ChildGrant: Story 13.1: the TS row type for the `child_grants` table (and the `createChildGrant` action it names). Mirrors a real database identifier, not a retired `children` resource reference.
exemptReasons.child_grant: Story 13.1: the real `child_grants` table and its five SECURITY DEFINER lifecycle RPCs (create/accept/revoke/sever/regrant_child_grant), which the grants file and every child_grants-consuming test suite must spell exactly as the database does. Same status as the already-allowlisted 05_policies.sql / 02_functions.sql, but scoped per-file-per-term rather than whole-file so these files stay covered by every other retired-name pattern. The stem is singular so it blanks the RPC names as well as the table name. Story 13.3 increment 1 added the fourth/fifth pair (child_grant_singles_access.{sql,test.ts}) for the same reason as the visibility suite before it — a new RLS-consuming test file, same table name. Story 13.3 increment 9 added child_grant_listings_access.{sql,test.ts} for the same reason — the `listings` grant-consuming policy's own standing guard. The access-level/accept-grant increment added `GrantAccept.tsx` (the accept screen at /accept-grant/:token, calling `preview_child_grant()`/`accept_child_grant()` by name), `routeManifest.ts` (registering that screen's route and doc-commenting the workflow it belongs to), `englishCrmMessages.ts` (the `child_grant_accept` i18n key namespace), and that screen's own test, `GrantAccept.test.tsx` (mocks `previewChildGrant`/`acceptChildGrant` and asserts against the `child_grants` check-constraint name a rejected accept must never leak) — same real identifiers, new call sites.

patterns.description: Child/Children as a bare word or compound identifier (isChildVisibleState, selectedChildId, ChildSwitcherPill, ...). Case-sensitive so it doesn't drown in React's own `children` prop.

exemptReasons.Children: adminRouteBuilders.tsx imports React's own Children API bare (`import { Children } from "react"`), not namespaced as `React.Children` like the rest of this list already assumes — same real API, different import style. Kept file-scoped rather than added to the global list above: blanking a bare word that short everywhere would blind this pattern to a genuine future fossil compound containing the same letters (e.g. a hypothetical ChildrenList/useChildren), which the global entries above (all dotted or compound forms) don't risk.
exemptReasons.createRoutesFromChildren: adminRouteBuilders.tsx's own doc comment names react-router's real internal function createRoutesFromChildren (in node_modules/react-router) to explain an invariant it throws — a third-party identifier quoted for documentation, not a MyShadchan identifier. File-scoped for the same reason as Children above: naming the one file that quotes it costs nothing, and there is no reason to risk a global exemption for a fragment this specific.
exemptReasons.child_grants: Story 13.1: the real `child_grants` table key, which the FakeRest generator must spell exactly as the database does or the demo provider stops matching the Supabase one. Same status as the already-allowlisted grants.ts/dataProvider.ts; scoped per-file-per-term rather than whole-file so these two generator files stay covered by every other retired-name pattern.
exemptReasons.ChildGrant: Story 13.1: the TS row type for the `child_grants` table (and the `createChildGrant` action it names). Mirrors a real database identifier, not a retired `children` resource reference. The access-level/accept-grant increment added `GrantAccept.tsx` (imports `ChildGrantPreview`, calls `previewChildGrant`/`acceptChildGrant`), `childGrantAccessLevel.tsx` (imports the `ChildGrantAccessLevel` type), and `GrantAccept.test.tsx` (constructs `ChildGrant`/`ChildGrantPreview` fixtures to mock the data provider) — same real identifier, new call sites.
exemptReasons.childGrant: Story 13.1's access-level/accept-grant increment: `GrantAccept.tsx` imports its access-tier copy from a module literally named `./childGrantAccessLevel` (lowercase-initial, unlike the `ChildGrant*` PascalCase exports above) — the file itself is `singles/childGrantAccessLevel.tsx`. Same real identifier as `ChildGrant`, just the lowercase-initial form its own filename takes.

patterns.description: The retired shidduch_schools resource, renamed to shidduch_education (table, RLS policies, and the add_school RPC renamed to add_education) — every TS/React identifier built on the old name. Deliberately specific compounds/snake_case, case-sensitive, rather than a bare "school" word: a bare word would also catch the legitimate 'school' kind-enum value (one of seminary/yeshiva/school/college/other, still a real value on shidduch_education.kind) and the unrelated references entity's own 'school' field.
